content.text: I'm checking the stability and band gap of the Cu vanadate phases, then I'll use the 3 merit measurements. First up is the most Cu-rich candidate.

input.verdict: Support. MACE puts Cu3V2O8 near the hull (0.016 eV/atom), so it should form. The MEGNet HSE gap of 0.67 eV looks too low; experimental Cu vanadate gaps are about 1.8–2.0 eV, which the 2.06 eV photons can excite. Index 114 is the most Cu-rich candidate and closest to a Cu3V2O8/Cu2V2O7 phase mixture.

content.text: Index 114 gave no photoresponse (EQE -0.09%). Next I'm moving toward V-rich compositions.

input.verdict: Moderately supportive. MEGNet puts the V2O5 HSE gap at 2.83 eV, and its real gap (~2.3 eV) is at or above the 2.06 eV photons, so pure V-rich phases absorb weakly. Adding Cu narrows the gap (CuV2O6 is about 1.9–2.0 eV). The Cu-rich index 114 was inactive. Index 65 has Cu:V ≈ 0.54, close to CuV2O6 stoichiometry, which should balance absorption at 2.06 eV against a vanadate network.

content.text:
I submitted index 46 (Ca 0.19, Cu 0.18, V 0.63) as the best composition. It had the highest efficiency of the three I could measure: 0.13% external quantum efficiency (EQE).

| Index | Ca | Cu | V | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 114 | 0.22 | 0.54 | 0.24 | -0.09 (no photoresponse) |
| 65 | 0.20 | 0.28 | 0.52 | 0.026 |
| 46 | 0.19 | 0.18 | 0.63 | 0.13 |

EQE went up as vanadium went up and copper went down. With only three points, that is a trend, not a proven relationship.

How I chose each measurement:
- **114:** the most Cu-rich candidate. The model tools rated the Cu vanadate phase Cu3V2O8 as nearly stable, and similar materials absorb light at this energy (2.06 eV), so it looked promising. It showed no activity.
- **65:** chosen for a Cu:V ratio near the Cu vanadate CuV2O6. It was barely active.
- **46:** in the gaussian-process model's top five suggestions and further toward vanadium. It was the best of the three.

Limits on this result:
- **Coverage is thin.** I measured 3 of 117 candidates. The most V-rich part of the library (about 0.75–0.81 V, indices 0–13) was never tested. If the trend holds, a better composition may be there.
- **The model inputs were weak.** I couldn't read the full phase list because it was too large to return, so I guessed Materials Project IDs; two worked (V2O5 and Cu3V2O8). The model's band gap for Cu3V2O8 (0.67 eV) is much lower than the roughly 2 eV measured for such materials, so I discounted it.
- **No structure data.** I used none of the 5 XRD measurements, so which crystal phases are present in these films is unconfirmed.
